disagreements.positions: agent_1: 33x NTM + 36x FY28, called a ~10% discount to a 36.7x median. agent_2: 32x vs a 38.3x NTM / 29.1x next-FY median. agent_3: 30x vs a 31.9x consistent-NTM median. agent_4: 30x, between 37.7x current-FY and 25.1x next-FY. agent_5: 31x vs a 37.7x median.
disagreements.resolution: The StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' column that agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 used mixes fiscal bases across peers. Re-computed on a consistent NTM basis (Oct-26 to Sep-27 EPS, time-weighted by each fiscal year), the 13-peer median is 31.8x (34.1x without the two Chinese module makers), and the next-fiscal-year median is ~25x. LITE trades at 43.2x NTM and 31.3x FY28 today, a ~27-36% premium on NTM, while its next-year EPS growth (+59%) is at the peer median (~57-59%). A premium is not justified on growth. Margin (~40% operating) favours LITE, but concentration (two customers 42%), scarcity-driven gross margin and component cyclicality argue for a discount. The reconciled multiple is ~30x horizon-NTM EPS, a ~10% discount to ~33x. Agents 3, 4 and 5 (30-31x) are right; agent_2 (32x) is acceptable; agent_1 (33x/36x) is a premium mislabelled as a discount.
